answer: I can’t name a guaranteed cheapest model without live pricing and official support data, because prices and firmware support change. To find the lowest-cost hardware wallet that still handles Ethereum and Solana: 1) Check the manufacturer’s official supported-assets page for your exact model and firmware version—both ETH and SOL must be listed. 2) Prefer entry-level models from established brands, but confirm Solana is supported natively or through a trusted companion app; some devices support ETH only. 3) Buy only from the official store or authorized reseller to avoid tampered devices. 4) Compare total cost: device, shipping, cables, and any required app. 5) Confirm you can restore with a standard seed phrase, use a passphrase if desired, and manage SPL tokens/staking if needed. Tradeoff: hardware wallets keep keys offline and require physical confirmation, which is safer for larger holdings, but cost more and are less convenient. Mobile/software wallets are free or cheap and convenient for small amounts, but keys live on an internet-connected device, so risk is higher. If budget is very tight, use a reputable software wallet for small funds, or save for a hardware wallet whose official specs clearly list Ethereum and Solana.
